subject.title: fix: sleep tool — session-targeted wake, correct sandbox policy, doc fixes

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool as a cron-backed session-targeted wake, or require a dedicated gateway resume primitive before merge?
rationale: This adds a new model-facing core scheduling tool across Gateway cron, session-state, interruption, restart, and sandbox-policy boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/API shape.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core sleep tool
options.body: Accept the feature direction, but require the supported Gateway scheduling API, consistent tool schema, live same-session proof, and explicit sandbox policy before merge.

options.title: Require a dedicated resume primitive
options.body: Pause this cron-wrapper approach until Gateway owns an explicit self-pause/resume contract with interruption and restart semantics.

options.title: Keep current cron guidance
options.body: Reject the new core tool for now and keep delayed work on the existing cron, process, and `sessions_yield` surfaces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core sleep tool
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction, but require the supported Gateway scheduling API, consistent tool schema, live same-session proof, and explicit sandbox policy before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the agent tool registry, Gateway call contract, cron targeting, and sandbox-policy surface.
